title: Oil & Water
briefing: Amsterdam. Nine hundred thousand people, almost as many bicycles, and a hundred kilometres of canals that have carried other people's money for four centuries.
The money meant for CINDER didn't vanish with the island. It is being washed through paint.

A forger known only as De Meester turns out Golden Age masters that were never painted. Margriet Ostendorp sells them under the hammer at the Gulden Hamer to buyers who don't exist. Sem Kooistra takes the proceeds out through the canals in uncut stones.
Tonight is the autumn sale. All three will be within half a kilometre of each other, and none of them will stand still.
Remove all three. If you can, bring us the Gulden Hamer's ledger. Be gone before the bells strike nine.

targets.name: Margriet Ostendorp
targets.desc: Auctioneer. Runs tonight's sale at the Gulden Hamer, never alone.

targets.name: De Meester
targets.desc: The forger. Nobody knows his face; he paints among his apprentices.

targets.name: Sem Kooistra
targets.desc: Smuggler. Rides his salon boat round the canals and can't swim.

intel: Catering at the Gulden Hamer is brought in. Nobody checks the faces of the waiters, but everybody checks their bags.
The guest list is for bidders. A bidder's paddle opens every door the public may use.
There is a metal detector inside the Gulden Hamer's front doors. Guns and anything sharp set it off, unless you wear a guard's uniform. Staff and caterers come in through the garden door.
De Meester never signs his work. His apprentices say he is the only one who paints left-handed.
Watch the four painters at work long enough and he gives himself away. Or read the café's wage book: In de Gouden Ton pays his apprentices, and one name draws no wage.
Twice an evening De Meester goes down to the quay for air, right under the hoist with the lead white.
Ostendorp takes her champagne in the private viewing room. Kooistra keeps a bottle of jenever in his cabin.
The saleroom chandelier hangs on a rope from the press balcony. Ostendorp stands under it for every lot.
The Gulden Hamer's ledger is kept in the strongbox in the basement vault.
A bidder's paddle from the reception desk gets you into the saleroom without questions.
There is turpentine in the forger's studio. Stoves don't like it.
The bridge keeper and the lock keeper lock their panels. Their keys are in the booth and the lock house.
Kooistra can't swim. His salon boat, the Zwaluw, takes him from his houseboat on the Gildegracht through the drawbridge, up to the smuggler's dock, out on the IJ and home again through the lock.
The bridge keeper raises the Gildegracht drawbridge for any boat that sounds its horn twice. Boats wait for it under the goods crane on the south quay. The lever in her booth holds the bridge down.
The lock keeper's sluice wheel empties the lock chamber all at once. Nobody should be standing at the rail when it does.

points.say: Lot nine opens at four hundred. Not a cent less.
Welcome, welcome. The catalogue is on the table.
Between us: the provenance is impeccable.
Lot nine. A merchant's daughter, sixteen-sixty. Do I hear four hundred?
Four hundred, the gentleman by the window. Four-fifty?
Sold. Lot ten, a winter landscape with skaters.
Write it in the book. Every lot, every buyer.
Champagne, while they find their chequebooks.
Turpentine. It gets into your head after a while.
He never signs them. Says the paint signs itself.
Weather like this, nobody looks at the water.
Count it twice. Then once more.
Hollandse nieuwe! Fresh in this morning.

events.text: The bell rings in the Gulden Hamer: bidders to the saleroom.
events.sub: The sale starts at a quarter to.

events.text: The sale begins. Ostendorp takes the podium.
events.sub: She stays at the lectern until a quarter past.

events.text: The sale breaks for the interval.
events.sub: Ostendorp goes down to the vault, then upstairs for champagne.
